findings.text: The enclave initialization entry validates lifecycle state before accepting user data, requiring creation already recorded and initialization not yet recorded. It copies a small argument block from user space, allocates one page to hold signature and token areas with token placed at half page offset and zeroed launch token area, copies the signature from user address, rejects vendor values outside two legacy allowances, then delegates to internal initialization and releases the allocation.

The provisioning entry copies a descriptor from user space and forwards its file reference to attribute gating. Gating accepts only a live descriptor whose operations match the provisioning file operations, and on success records permission for the provisioning key attribute in the caller supplied mask.

Two SGX2 permission and type change entries share a readiness gate that requires processor SGX2 support and completed enclave initialization. Each copies its parameter block, validates enclave offset and byte count alignment and range, checks that requested permission or type bits stay within allowed masks and that result and progress outputs start cleared, delegates to an internal worker, then copies updated result and progress back to user space.

Security info validation accepts only regular and thread control page types, rejects write permission without read permission, requires zero permissions for thread control entries because hardware silently clears them, rejects any reserved flag bits, and rejects any nonzero reserved bytes. Any violation yields an invalid argument failure.

Offset and length validation requires page aligned offset, nonzero page aligned length, no unsigned wrap of the sum, and containment of the final page within enclave extent. Violations yield invalid argument.

Page allocation creates a zeroed tracking object whose guest address equals enclave base plus supplied offset and whose owner points back to the enclave. Requested security permission bits translate into maximum virtual memory protections for read write and execute, with thread control pages forced to readable and writable for processor access despite zero security permissions, and the combined ceiling stored as protection bits.

The low level add helper denies executable source absence by locating the virtual area covering the user source address and requiring may execute capability, pins a single source page, prepares a page info bundle linking enclave control plus page aligned destination plus security metadata plus temporarily mapped source contents, issues the hardware add leaf EADD against fresh enclave memory, then unmaps and releases the source page and maps hardware failure to input output error.

The outer add sequence allocates tracking plus enclave memory plus version array resources before taking locks, then under address space read lock and enclave mutex links any new version page, inserts the tracking object into the indexed page collection keyed by guest frame before hardware action to preserve measurability on allocation failure, performs hardware add, and only then completes linkage, records page type from security flags, increments child accounting and optionally measures. Success marks memory reclaimable. Failure removes the index entry, releases version growth, frees memory and tracking, with distinct unwind paths for pre and post index insertion.

Measurement walks a full page in fixed size blocks issuing the hardware extend leaf EEXTEND for each chunk from enclave control against successive offsets, warning on architectural failure and converting any failure to input output error.

Internal initialization denies enclave attributes outside the allowed mask with access failure, denies signature requested attributes plus misc selection plus extended features that intersect platform reserved masks when also enabled by their masks, and hashes the signature modulus to derive signer identity. Vendor filtering for legacy values occurs in the outer entry.

Initialization executes the hardware init leaf EINIT under enclave mutex with preemption disabled around launch key hash refresh and leaf invocation, retrying inner spins then outer sleeps when hardware reports an unmasked event to service interrupts, aborting with restartable signal status if a signal becomes pending during sleep. Architectural faults map to input output error with warning on failure, other nonzero hardware codes map to permission failure with debug logging, and success records initialized state.
Launch key hash refresh asserts nonpreemptible context and programs four consecutive model specific registers starting at MSR_IA32_SGXLEPUBKEYHASH0 with supplied words.

Permission restriction iterates the requested byte range page by page, opportunistically reclaiming before each page, loading or faulting in the page under enclave mutex, allowing only regular pages, issuing the hardware permission change leaf EMODPR with permission only security info, classifying architectural traps as faults and other hardware failures as reported status, then performing tracking synchronization before releasing the mutex. Progress count reflects completed bytes and result carries hardware status on failure.

Page load resolves guest frame in the indexed collection, faults when absent, returns immediately when enclave memory already attached unless concurrently reclaiming in which case it reports busy, otherwise ensures control page resident then reloads through hardware leaf ELDU with fresh enclave memory, updates child accounting and reclaim tracking. Successful reload releases the version slot, recycles its version page to the available list, clears version offset bits and attaches new memory.

Reload from backing derives a page index from guest offset or enclave size for control, computes first page sharing the same metadata page and metadata offset, maps content and metadata pages through temporary mappings, issues hardware reload with control address or zero for control itself, then clears the used metadata entry, dirties the metadata page, releases mappings and backing references, truncates the content page, and conditionally truncates the metadata page only when fully zero and no sibling in the same group is concurrently reclaiming, warning if truncation leaves residue.

Tracking synchronization issues the hardware track leaf ETRACK against enclave control, and on failure logs once, broadcasts an interprocessor kick to enclave CPUs and retries once before failing. On success it always broadcasts the same kick after the leaf. Direct reclaim checks a low page threshold and triggers reclamation when needed.

Address space read lock nests outside enclave mutex during page addition, with version list and index mutations plus hardware add and extend all covered by the mutex. Initialization holds the mutex across the full retry loop. Permission changes lock per page around load plus permission leaf plus tracking. Reclaimer spin lock protects tracked flag and active list linkage. Version page list add plus move plus shrink require mutex. Launch key programming requires preemption disabled.

Observed enclave state includes base plus size plus lock plus indexed page collection plus version page list plus control tracking plus child count plus attribute set and mask plus flags plus backing reference. Observed page tracking includes guest descriptor with address plus version offset and reclaim flag plus owner pointer plus enclave memory pointer plus type plus version page pointer plus maximum protection bits. Observed hardware bundles include page info with control plus guest address plus metadata plus content addresses and security info with flags and reserved area.

Enclave progresses from created to initialized exactly once. Initialization entry rejects when creation absent or initialization already present, and internal success sets initialized. SGX2 permission and type operations require initialized plus processor feature. Attribute mask starts restrictive and gains provisioning key only through provisioning gate. Initialization enforces attributes against mask.

Page tracking moves from allocated to indexed to hardware added to linked and reclaimable, with optional measurement between linkage and reclaimable marking. Reclaim detaches enclave memory while retaining index plus backing plus version slot. Reload reallocates memory, clears version linkage and returns to reclaimable. Control page follows same reload path with zero control link and size derived index. Child count increments on add and reload.

Hardware add updates measurement and cannot be unwound, requiring index insertion beforehand. Thread control permissions are silently cleared by hardware so software must validate zero. Initialization leaf is long latency and interruptible, requiring retry on unmasked events. Permission change faults on nonregular pages and requires prior validation plus serialized access to avoid concurrent leaf faults. Double tracking without intervening processor kick fails. Metadata page truncation races with concurrent sibling reclaim and must be guarded by group scan.

Hardware and ABI identifiers observed include permission and page type masks plus regular versus control types plus write read execute permission bits plus reserved mask plus measure flag plus extend block stepping plus launch token size plus modulus size plus four word signer hash plus launch key hash register base plus vendor allowances zero and Intel identifier 0x0000 and 0x8086 plus enclave flags for created and initialized plus busy and reclaim signaling plus version offset mask and being reclaimed flag plus reclaim tracked flag plus low page threshold plus init sleep and spin counts plus regular page type and page type mask plus thirty two 32 metadata entries per page.

Helpers with external linkage provide page allocation with protection ceiling derivation plus page load by guest address with fault in plus marking enclave memory reclaimable plus direct reclaim threshold check plus launch key hash programming plus attribute mask extension for provisioning. Permission restriction worker is also externally visible and reports per range result and progress.

Thin wrappers bind each SGX leaf to its architectural number with fixed operand arity. Add and extend take two pointers. Permission change and two operand returning leaves take security info plus address. Reload takes page info plus two addresses. Init takes signature plus control plus token. A macro maps two operand returning leaves onto a generic variadic invocation with base and counter registers.
